tools.name: tokensave_search
tools.description: Search for symbols (functions, structs, traits, etc.) in the code graph by name or keyword. Persistent noise (vendored trees, docs) can be suppressed project-wide via gitignore-style patterns in .tokensave/queryignore.

query.description: Search query string to match against symbol names

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 10)

path_include.description: Only include results whose file path contains one of these substrings (e.g. "src", "app"). Empty/absent means no path constraint.

path_exclude.description: Exclude results whose file path contains any of these substrings (e.g. "node_modules", "dist", "venv"). Takes precedence over path_include.

literal.description: Exact-substring search over source text (for runtime error strings); returns file/line locations instead of ranked symbols, plus `total` matches and `truncated` when `limit` cut the list. Case-sensitive. Default false.

format.description: Output format. 'text' returns raw source with a short header (no JSON escaping); 'json' returns the structured object. Default 'text'.

ids.description: Include node IDs / enclosing IDs in results (both formats). Default false; pass true when you plan a follow-up call.

exact_total.description: Literal mode only. Count every match in the project, not just the ones shown, so `total` is exact. Default true. Pass false to stop the scan as soon as `limit` matches are found: the scan then reads only part of the project and `total` becomes a lower bound, reported as `total_exact: false`.

timeout_ms.description: Literal mode only. Give up on the scan after this many milliseconds and answer with the matches found so far, marked `timed_out: true` and `total_exact: false`. Default 30000; 0 disables the limit.

graph_root.description: Absolute root of another initialized project to query, or an array of roots to query together. Omit for the served project.

graph_branch.description: Tracked branch to query within graph_root. Requires graph_root.

tools.name: tokensave_context
tools.description: Build an AI-ready context for a task description. Returns relevant symbols, relationships, and optionally code snippets. The output includes a `### Retrieval` section: when it lists zero-hit terms, re-query once with `keywords` synonyms for them (or use tokensave_search); a `match: fts-only` tier means weak lexical matches, so verify entry points before building on them.

task.description: Natural language description of the task or question

max_nodes.description: Maximum number of symbols to include (default: 20)

include_code.description: If true, include source code snippets for key symbols (default: false)

max_code_blocks.description: Maximum number of code snippets when include_code is true (default: 5)

max_code_lines.description: Maximum lines per code snippet (default: unlimited, max 1000). Use it to see the signature plus the first lines of several symbols instead of one whole large body. A separate size limit of ~1500 bytes per snippet always applies, so a high line cap has little effect — asking for 100 lines does not guarantee 100 lines. Truncated snippets name the tokensave_body call that returns the rest.

mode.description: Context mode: 'explore' (default) for general exploration, 'plan' for implementation planning (adds extension points, dependency order, test coverage)

keywords.description: Extra search keywords for synonym expansion. Use this when the task uses conceptual terms that may not match symbol names — e.g. for 'authentication', pass ["login", "session", "credential", "token", "auth"]. The graph is searched for each keyword independently.

exclude_node_ids.description: Node IDs to exclude from results (pass seen_node_ids from previous call for session deduplication)

merge_adjacent.description: When true, merge code blocks from the same file whose line ranges are adjacent or overlapping (default: false)

max_per_file.description: Maximum symbols from a single file in results. Prevents one large file from dominating (default: max_nodes/3, minimum 3)

path_include.description: Only include results whose file path contains one of these substrings (e.g. "src", "app"). Empty/absent means no path constraint.

path_exclude.description: Exclude results whose file path contains any of these substrings (e.g. "node_modules", "dist", "venv"). Takes precedence over path_include.

graph_root.description: Absolute root of another initialized project to query. Omit for the served project.

graph_branch.description: Tracked branch to query within graph_root. Requires graph_root.

tools.name: tokensave_callers
tools.description: Find callers of a given node (function, method, etc.). Returns direct callers by default; pass max_depth > 1 to also follow the chain transitively. Each result includes `depth` (1 = direct caller, 2+ = transitive), `line` (the call-site line where the caller invokes the target), `lines` (every line where the caller invokes the target, ascending; a caller is listed once even when it calls the target several times), and `def_line`/`end_line` (the caller's own span). Generic callers through a trait are included for concrete impl methods and tagged with `dispatch_via_trait: true`; pass `resolve_dispatch: false` to disable reverse dispatch resolution. Pass `node_id`, or `symbol` to name the target directly: each match is answered in its own group (`symbol`, `match_count`, `matches[]` with the callers under `callers`), up to `max_matches`.

node_id.description: The unique node ID to find callers for. Takes precedence over `symbol`; one of the two is required.

symbol.description: Symbol name to find callers for instead of node_id (e.g. 'RefreshAsync'). Resolved as tokensave_body resolves it: 'Coordinator.RefreshAsync', 'Coordinator::RefreshAsync' and 'App.Coordinator.RefreshAsync' all work (trailing segments are matched), and a function or type outranks a same-named field or import. Overloads are answered together.

max_matches.description: When `symbol` matches several symbols, answer up to this many, each in its own group headed by qualified name, kind, file, line, end_line and node_id (default: 3, max: 20). Further matches are listed without results, in tokensave_search rank order, for a follow-up call by node_id.

limit.description: Maximum callers listed per match (default: 50, max: 500). When more exist, the result reports `count`, `total` and `truncated: true` (with node_id alone, the list is then wrapped as `{count, total, truncated, callers}`).

max_depth.description: Maximum traversal depth, 1-10 (default: 1 = direct callers only). Higher values also return transitive callers, each tagged with its `depth`.

resolve_dispatch.description: If true (default), include generic callers that invoke the corresponding trait method.

graph_root.description: Absolute root of another initialized project to query. Omit for the served project.

graph_branch.description: Tracked branch to query within graph_root. Requires graph_root.

tools.name: tokensave_callees
tools.description: Find all callees of a given node (function, method, etc.) up to a specified depth. When a callee resolves to a trait method, the concrete impl methods reachable through that trait are also returned, tagged with `dispatch_via_trait: true` and a `dispatch_from` pointing at the trait method. Pass `resolve_dispatch: false` to disable this behaviour and get only direct call edges. Pass `node_id`, or `symbol` to name the target directly: each match is answered in its own group (`symbol`, `match_count`, `matches[]` with the callees under `callees`), up to `max_matches`.

node_id.description: The unique node ID to find callees for. Takes precedence over `symbol`; one of the two is required.

symbol.description: Symbol name to find callees for instead of node_id (e.g. 'RefreshAsync'). Resolved as tokensave_body resolves it: 'Coordinator.RefreshAsync', 'Coordinator::RefreshAsync' and 'App.Coordinator.RefreshAsync' all work (trailing segments are matched), and a function or type outranks a same-named field or import. Overloads are answered together.

max_matches.description: When `symbol` matches several symbols, answer up to this many, each in its own group headed by qualified name, kind, file, line, end_line and node_id (default: 3, max: 20). Further matches are listed without results, in tokensave_search rank order, for a follow-up call by node_id.

limit.description: Maximum callees listed per match (default: 50, max: 500). When more exist, the result reports `count`, `total` and `truncated: true` (with node_id alone, the list is then wrapped as `{count, total, truncated, callees}`).

resolve_dispatch.description: If true (default), append concrete impl methods for any trait-method callee.

graph_root.description: Absolute root of another initialized project to query. Omit for the served project.

graph_branch.description: Tracked branch to query within graph_root. Requires graph_root.

tools.name: tokensave_impact
tools.description: Compute the impact radius of a node: all symbols that directly or indirectly depend on it. Pass `node_id`, or `symbol` to name the target directly: each match is answered in its own group (`symbol`, `match_count`, `matches[]`), up to `max_matches`. `node_count` is the full radius; `nodes` lists at most `limit` of them.

node_id.description: The unique node ID to compute impact for. Takes precedence over `symbol`; one of the two is required.

symbol.description: Symbol name to compute impact for instead of node_id (e.g. 'RefreshAsync'). Resolved as tokensave_body resolves it: 'Coordinator.RefreshAsync', 'Coordinator::RefreshAsync' and 'App.Coordinator.RefreshAsync' all work (trailing segments are matched), and a function or type outranks a same-named field or import. Overloads are answered together.

max_matches.description: When `symbol` matches several symbols, answer up to this many, each in its own group headed by qualified name, kind, file, line, end_line and node_id (default: 3, max: 20). Further matches are listed without results, in tokensave_search rank order, for a follow-up call by node_id.

limit.description: Maximum nodes listed per match (default: 50, max: 500). When more exist, the result reports `count`, `total` and `truncated: true`.

graph_root.description: Absolute root of another initialized project to query. Omit for the served project.

graph_branch.description: Tracked branch to query within graph_root. Requires graph_root.

tools.name: tokensave_files
tools.description: List indexed project files, including non-code artifacts such as .feature specs, schemas, and fixtures. Use to explore file structure, or to locate files by path pattern, without reading file contents.

path.description: Filter to files under this directory path

pattern.description: Filter files matching this glob pattern (e.g. '**/*.rs', '**/*.feature')

kind.description: Filter by file kind: 'code' for parsed source files, 'artifact' for non-code files tracked by path only (specs, schemas, fixtures, docs). Omit for both.

format.description: Output format: flat (one per line) or grouped by directory (default: grouped)

graph_root.description: Absolute root of another initialized project to query, or an array of roots to query together. Omit for the served project.

graph_branch.description: Tracked branch to query within graph_root. Requires graph_root.

tools.name: tokensave_str_replace
tools.description: Replace a unique string in a file with new content. Fails if the old string is not found or matches more than once. This is the safest edit primitive — use this instead of sed/awk.

path.description: Absolute or project-relative file path. An absolute path is always honored verbatim, even outside the indexed project root (e.g. a git worktree).

old_str.description: Exact string to find and replace. Must match exactly once in the file.

project_root.description: Optional absolute directory to resolve a relative `path` against instead of the indexed project root, e.g. a git worktree. Ignored when `path` is absolute. Alias: `cwd`.

echo.description: If true, echo the replaced/inserted text in the result. Default false.

tools.name: tokensave_multi_str_replace
tools.description: Apply multiple string replacements atomically in a single file. All replacements must match exactly once. If any replacement fails (0 or >1 matches), the entire operation is aborted and no changes are made.

path.description: Absolute or project-relative file path. An absolute path is always honored verbatim, even outside the indexed project root (e.g. a git worktree).

replacements.description: Array of [old_str, new_str] pairs to replace

project_root.description: Optional absolute directory to resolve a relative `path` against instead of the indexed project root, e.g. a git worktree. Ignored when `path` is absolute. Alias: `cwd`.

tools.name: tokensave_body
tools.description: Return the full source body of a symbol by name (function, struct, const, etc.). Collapses search + node lookup + file read into a single call. Returns a body only when exactly one definition matches; when the name is ambiguous (e.g. several methods named `RefreshAsync`), returns no body but a candidate list (qualified name, kind, file, line range, node id) — re-call with a qualified name such as `Type::Member` / `Type.Member`, or with `node_id`. A function or type definition outranks a same-named field or import.

symbol.description: Symbol name to look up (e.g. 'resolve_provider_api_key', 'GraphStats'). Qualify it to disambiguate: 'Coordinator::RefreshAsync', 'Coordinator.RefreshAsync' and 'App.Coordinator.RefreshAsync' all work (trailing segments are matched).

node_id.description: Node id of the symbol (from a candidate list, tokensave_search, or tokensave_context). Takes precedence over `symbol`.

limit.description: Maximum number of candidates listed when the name is ambiguous (default: 20, max: 50)

format.description: Output format. 'text' returns raw source with a short header (no JSON escaping); 'json' returns the structured object. Default 'text'.

graph_root.description: Absolute root of another initialized project to query. Omit for the served project.

graph_branch.description: Tracked branch to query within graph_root. Requires graph_root.

tools.name: tokensave_read
tools.description: Read a file or its symbol map. Modes: 'full' (entire file), 'lines' (1-based inclusive line-range slice via the 'lines' arg, e.g. '120-180'), 'map' (flat list of every top-level symbol from the graph — no source bytes touched), 'signatures' (functions and types with their cached signature). 'full' and 'lines' number every line like the Read tool: right-aligned real file line number, a tab, then the line (a 'lines' slice from 120 starts at 120). The body is always returned, with a 'digest' of it. To skip re-sending content you still hold, pass that digest as 'if_digest': when it matches the current body for the same mode and range, a tiny stub with 'unchanged: true' is returned instead.

file.description: Project-relative or absolute path to the file (e.g. 'src/sync.rs'). Alias: `path`.

lines.description: Required when mode='lines'. Format 'A-B' or single 'A' (1-based, inclusive). E.g. '120-180' or '42'. Or pass `start` and `end` (1-based line numbers; `end` defaults to the end of the file).

if_digest.description: Digest from an earlier tokensave_read response with the same mode and range that you still hold. If it matches the current content, an 'unchanged: true' stub is returned instead of the body; otherwise the body is returned. Omit to always get the body.

force.description: Deprecated: the body is now always returned unless 'if_digest' matches. When true, 'if_digest' is ignored. Default false.

format.description: Output format. 'text' returns raw source with a short header (no JSON escaping); 'json' returns the structured object. Default 'text'.

graph_root.description: Absolute root of another initialized project to query. Omit for the served project.

graph_branch.description: Tracked branch to query within graph_root. Requires graph_root.

tools.name: tokensave_more
tools.description:
List more tokensave tools. Only the core tools are listed at the start, to keep the tool schemas small. Call this with an area, and the tools of that area are listed from then on. Areas:
• analysis — code-quality metrics and audits: complexity, coupling, cycles, dead code, hotspots, health, test risk and coverage, diagnostics, package dependencies
• edit — symbol-level and line-level edits, ast-grep rewrite, graph-based rename
• git — commit, PR, diff, blame, log and changelog context, affected tests, tracked branches
• memory — session notes and recorded decisions
• navigate — more symbol lookups: node, signature, implementations, type hierarchy, imports, call chains, field and constructor sites
